description: Short concrete roadside post with a rounded white-painted top and a red band, showing distance to the next town.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Short squat concrete post set directly in the ground, square in section through its lower body and rounded over into a smooth domed top, the dome painted white with a large black numeral 42 on it, a single broad red horizontal band around the post below the dome, black lettering on the flat front face below the band reading the Thai place name สระบุรี above a smaller roman line reading SARABURI Materials: Whitewashed concrete gone grey and grimy at the base with soil splash, red band paint chalky and flaking, chipped corners exposing coarse aggregate, moss in the ground joint.

Legend: this object is a SIGN, and its printed legend is part of the object, not an annotation on the photograph. Render every letter, numeral, pictogram, arrow and coloured band described above, exactly as described and nothing more. Thai script must be rendered as Thai script with correct glyph shapes, above the roman line where both are described. Lettering and pictograms lie flat on the sign face, sharp, high-contrast and correctly proportioned, and the face must stay legible despite the camera angle. Do not leave the face blank, do not substitute lorem or invented wording, and do not add any text that was not described.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no drop shadow, and no border around the photograph itself.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

featureReviews.evidence: The named gap of the previous review, scored 0.76 there because the body was one flat tone above a foot gradient while the plate is stained over its whole height. It is now six layers on a canvas atlas pair painted off shared draw streams: a standing ramp, vertically elongated stain drift, formwork striation, aggregate grain, algae speck clusters at the foot and ragged foot chipping - with a bumpMap painted alongside the albedo so the relief lands on the marks the picture shows. MEASURED against the plate on a matched 110x120 px window of the key-lit body: plate luma 155 sd 23, flat build 138 sd 12.6, this build 154 sd 19.3. The deterministic material comparator moves deltaE00 2.96 -> 2.44, baseColor 0.941 -> 0.951 and directionalResponse 0.839 -> 0.944. Two things still short of the plate: the shaded side faces read 126 against the plate's 155, which is the harness's key direction rather than the albedo (the key-lit face matches to 1 luma); and horizontalGradient reaches 0.032 against the plate's 0.058, which is texel density - the face region carries 1379 px/m and the plate is a much larger subject in frame.

Every edge is a 22 mm three-segment bevel. The plate's crown turns over in the DEPTH axis as well as across the face - it is a rolled dome, not a barrel vault with a knife-edge perimeter - and the previous build's prismatic extrude with bevelEnabled false showed a hard silhouette edge at every azimuth. Normals are smoothed with an angle-limited pass at 62 degrees so the bevel rounds over while the flat faces stay flat; unconditional averaging is the LatheGeometry mistake that shades a dark ring the turntable gate reads as a hole. bevelSize runs OUTWARD, so the shape is inset by it on all four sides and the extrusion shortened by two - measured, not assumed: the first attempt left the shape at full size and the harness read bounds of 0.534 x 0.944. Bounds now read exactly 0.490 x 0.900 x 0.420. Arch segments 16 -> 24. 72 -> 428 triangles of 2000.

The previous build had fourteen axis-aligned rectangles along the band's lower edge, which rendered as a sawtooth graphic. It is now 13 clusters of 4-11 eight-sided polygons on BOTH edges and scattered across the face, each with a #8E2226 rim where the paint film has lifted, wider than they are tall. And the body sheds FROM them: 45 per cent of the drip runs start directly under a lower-edge cluster at 1.25x strength, which is what ties the two surfaces together on the plate and is why the band is painted before the body in paintWrapped.

Re-measured off the plate: the void spans y=735..870 on a stone spanning y=72..952, i.e. 0.093 to 0.247 of height, so it is centred at 0.17 and is 0.135 of the height tall - the previous build had it at 0.21 and half that size, as a flat grey ellipse. It is painted from the OUTSIDE IN now: a soft shadow spilling onto the wall, a #6B6047 void, then a small patch of lit #C8C1AE aggregate low inside it, with a matching recess in the height atlas. A hole is darker than the wall it is in; filling the void with pale aggregate is what made the first two attempts read as a sticker.

The atlas column was sampled at ONE u by every side wall and the back - a single texel column stretched across 0.42 m of stone - so nothing on three of the four faces could vary horizontally and every wash arrived as a full-width horizontal band. It is 0.30 of the atlas now, with a guard gutter flood-filled rather than left transparent, and the walls map their own horizontal position into it (a side wall along z, the back cap and crown along x). Mark sizes are then scaled by 0.40 and counts divided by it, because the column carries 1.37 mm per texel against the face's 0.54 and the same fraction is a mark 2.5x larger in the world.

The Thai line rendered as six tofu boxes in the harness and in the thumbnail it writes. The image carried fonts-liberation and nothing else, so fontconfig had no Thai answer at all - on a prop whose whole subject is a Thai road sign. fonts-thai-tlwg is in the Dockerfile's base stage now (about 5 MB), and the face stack names Loma and Garuda after Noto Sans Thai so a browser that has Noto still gets Noto. Verified in the render.

name: Kilometre Stone
nameTh: หลักกิโลเมตร
notes: Kept on the derived medium budget with no override, which is the right answer here: at 0.9 m the size rule gives 2 draw calls and 2 materials, and the real prop is exactly two surfaces, the whitewashed concrete body and the painted band. Collider stays the signage default box because the post is genuinely square in section through its body. Placement is overridden to floor rather than the signage default of wall, because this is a ground-set stone. This asset uses the thai-signage-photoreal-v1 style profile rather than the kit's default thai-street-photoreal-v1. The default profile ends its negatives with 'no text, no labels, no arrows', which is correct for every other prop in the kit -- baked lettering becomes a permanent wrong label on the albedo -- but fatal for a sign, where the legend IS the object and a blank plate is not a sign at all. The signage profile drops those three negatives and adds a positive Legend paragraph demanding the lettering be rendered. Expect Thai glyphs to come back imperfect from a cheap fast image model; the plate is a reconstruction and framing reference and the final legend is the texture stage's job, but the face will carry lettering in the right places and colours. The distance numeral and place name differ at every real instance, so a consumer placing a run of these along a highway should retexture the numeral per instance rather than repeat one stone -- the legend baked here is a representative example, not a fixed value. No destruction groups.
